prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph at golden hour in arctic conditions, 85mm medium-format camera on a helicopter mount looking down-angle at a glacier field. Crisp low-angle sun, sharp shadows, clear visibility.

Subject:
A kilometers-wide glacier made entirely of golden topaz rather than ice. Enormous honey-colored crystal slabs, fractured into chunks the size of apartment buildings, drift slowly through a fjord. Sunlight enters each slab and emerges as warm amber beams that project sharp-edged golden shapes onto the fjord water and the far cliff wall.

Important details:
Realistic topaz optical properties: strong dispersion, visible internal cleavage planes, surface sheen. Crystal slabs show realistic calving fractures at their edges, as if broken off a larger parent mass. Scale anchors: a small expedition helicopter hovering above one slab, and two kayaks threading between crystal chunks. Atmosphere: cold air shimmer, thin steam rising from the water where sunlight concentrates.

Use case:
Crystal-studies single 4/5 — the glacier itself is the impossible crystal material.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no ice (topaz replaces ice entirely), no polar bears, no branded outdoor gear, no stylized painting.
title: Topaz Glacier
description: A fjord full of building-sized topaz crystal slabs acting as an impossible golden glacier.
